title: Edge Install Execution Digest — Standup & Escalations (week of 2026-05-18)
content:
Purpose: working log for the ‘Edge Install Command Center’ for the week of 2026-05-18. Capture standup notes, active customer blockers, quick triage timeline, short-term mitigations, and explicit next steps. This is an operational working doc — rough notes and actions live here until we triage into JIRA tickets and runbook updates.

Summary (high level):
- Two active installs in parallel: Customer A (VPC, multi-AZ) and Customer B (on-prem rack install).
- Customer A: network / CIDR overlap discovered during preflight; resolving with Network team and customer security. Expected delay 48–72h for approval.
- Customer B: kernel driver mismatch on 4 out of 8 GPU nodes causing segfault in the runtime; mitigation path identified (downgrade container runtime + reprovision driver packages) — target rollback window scheduled tonight.

Attendees (standup 2026-05-18 09:30 PT):
- Priya Shah (Install lead)
- Lina Gomez (SRE, telemetry)
- Marcus Li (Solutions eng, on-prem lead)
- Asha Patel (Security & Network)
- Tom Weaver (Field PM)

09:30 — Rapid status check:
- Priya: quick recap of current installs and priorities. Asked for triage owners.
- Marcus: on-prem nodes failing smoke on gpu0–gpu3, kernel oops on container start (stack trace attached to PD-4821).
- Lina: metrics/agent reports show heartbeat gap 10:21–10:34 on Customer B; CNIs flapped after runtime start.
- Asha: Customer A has overlapping 10.0.0.0/16 prefix with upstream transit — waiting for SecOps approval for address remap.

Active Blockers (detail):
1) Customer A — VPC CIDR overlap (BLOCKER):
   - Observed: preflight validation flagged 10.0.0.0/16 overlap with existing transit peering. Customer must either provide alternate CIDR or approve NAT/proxy pattern.
   - Impact: install cannot proceed; provisioning of control-plane resources blocked.
   - Triage owner: Asha Patel.
   - Temporary mitigation: suggest using our private-subnet template with 172.21.0.0/16 as alternative; noted constraints with customer's internal routing appliances (firewalls).
   - Next steps: Asha to run a short network mapping session with customer network team today 14:00 PT. If customer approves, engineering to reapply templates by 15:30 PT and resume provisioning.
   - Risks/notes: multi-AZ placement requires non-overlapping CIDR for VPC peering; if customer cannot change CIDR, escalate to Field PM (Tom) for contract-level solution (dedicated transit or NAT gateway add-on).

2) Customer B — On-prem runtime segfaults after docker runtime upgrade (BLOCKER):
   - Observed: after nodes were patched overnight, 4/8 GPU nodes fail to start the inference container — kernel oops referencing nv_peer_mem and rmmalloc. Crash loop observed in containerd logs.
   - Triage owner: Marcus Li + Tom Weaver.
   - Investigation:
     - Lina pulled telemetry: driver version inconsistencies between nodes (535.112 vs 525.89).
     - Host driver 535 on failing nodes; our packaged runtime currently validated against 525.x.
     - Container runtime upgrade to containerd 1.8.6 changed cgroup handling — reproduces locally in lab.
   - Mitigation plan (short): schedule twilight rollback for container runtime to 1.7.11 on failing nodes (target 23:00 PT window). Also pin inference runtime to legacy compatibility mode (ENV:RW_FORCE_LEGACY_GPU=1) to bypass new allocations.
   - Longer-term: create an automated validation matrix to check host driver vs validated driver matrix before applying updates (ACTION: Priya to create PD epic).

3) Telemetry gaps / agent heartbeat drops (MEDIUM):
   - Observed intermittent heartbeats during install steps (workload bursts).
   - Lina: root cause appears to be a combination of high scheduling latency during heavy image pulls and the new agent's default flush interval.
   - Temporary change: increase agent flush interval from 5s to 15s and enable progressive backoff for telemetry uploads in the installer (config flag: agent.telemetry.backoff=true).
   - Action: Lina to push a small installer patch (PR 214) to include the backoff behavior. QA to smoke in lab before pushing to Customer B tonight.

Triage timeline (chronological):
- 2026-05-18 10:10 PT: Customer B support ticket opened (INFRA-1179).
- 2026-05-18 11:00 PT: Failed node snapshots collected and uploaded to S3 (link in JIRA).
- 2026-05-18 13:00 PT: Offline troubleshooting with on-site tech; determined host driver mismatch.
- 2026-05-18 14:00 PT: Network mapping call scheduled with Customer A (Asha + customer net team).
- 2026-05-18 16:30 PT: Internal sync — decided to hold Customer A provisioning until network approval.
- 2026-05-18 19:45 PT: Patch candidate for telemetry backoff created (github PR 214).
- 2026-05-18 20:30 PT: Night window reserved for Customer B rollback (23:00 PT start).

Night operations checklist (Customer B rollback window):
- Pre-window (22:30 PT): verify node snapshots & S3 uploads completed, confirm on-site tech availability.
- 22:45 PT: push annotated runbook steps to on-site tech (commands and expected outputs).
- 23:00 PT: perform containerd downgrade to 1.7.11 on failing nodes (commands below).
- 23:10 PT: restart inference runtime with RW_FORCE_LEGACY_GPU=1 and monitor logs for 15 minutes.
- 23:30 PT: run smoke test (end-to-end inference sample) on each recovered node and record latencies.
- 00:15 PT (approx): if stable, roll remaining nodes into production; if failure persists, fall back to cold standby in customer rack and initiate full driver reprovisioning.

Quick commands (for on-site tech) — note: use sudo where required:
- check driver: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
- downgrade containerd (example): apt-get install -y containerd=1.7.11-1 && systemctl restart containerd
- restart runtime (k8s): kubectl rollout restart daemonset/redwood-inference-runtime -n redwood
- collect logs: journalctl -u containerd -n 500 > /tmp/containerd-journal.log

Runbook gaps identified (to fix post-mortem):
- No explicit step for ‘host-driver vs packaged-runtime validation’ in current preflight; add a hard fail if driver > validated matrix.
- Installer does not currently auto-detect containerd versions during preflight (we rely on docs only). Add preflight check and documented remediation.
- Telemetry agent backoff/settings are not surfaced in the Console — make a short-term Console banner to warn about high-flush frequencies during installs.

Decisions & escalations made:
- Hold Customer A provisioning until network approval. If customer cannot change CIDR, field will propose dedicated transit (cost/lead time implications). (Owner: Tom)
- Rollback containerd on Customer B as immediate mitigation; follow-up with host-driver reprovisioning if rollback fails. (Owner: Marcus)
- Create PD epic to add a driver-version hard fail/preflight and update installer docs (Owner: Priya).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight compatibility table embedded in the installer (json) that maps validated host drivers/containerd versions to runtime images. It can be shipped as part of the helm chart and checked at install time.
- For VPC overlap cases, create a customer-ready one-pager that shows options (swap CIDR, NAT, dedicated transit) + time/cost impacts — this will speed Field conversations.

Open questions (unresolved):
- Customer A: will their security team allow 172.21.0.0/16 or prefer to purchase a dedicated transit route? Need answer by EOD 2026-05-19 to keep timeline.
- Customer B: do we have permission to reprovision GPU driver packages during business hours if rollback partially succeeds? Contract clause ambiguous; Tom to confirm.

Action items (short):
- Asha: run network mapping with customer (2026-05-18 14:00 PT) and report outcome in Slack.
- Marcus: prepare rollback runbook and remain on-call through window (23:00 PT).
- Lina: open PR 214 for telemetry backoff and coordinate quick QA.
- Priya: create PD epic and draft runbook updates; attach post-mortem template.
- Tom: escalate Customer A options to Field and set expectation with customer execs.

Appendix — artifacts and quick refs:
- PD-4821: Customer B failing nodes (contains core dumps & node snapshots).
- INFRA-1179: initial support ticket for Customer B.
- GH PR 214: installer telemetry backoff fix (linked above).

If anything changes after the 23:00 PT window or network call outcome, I will update this doc and move stable items into JIRA tickets. This is a working log — please add short notes inline and ping in #private-deploy for urgent updates.

— Priya
(working doc; will convert to final post-mortem or runbook update after stabilizing installs)
